cards.text: Right before this, Wisdom cries aloud in the street for the simple ones to listen (Proverbs 1:20-22). Now the writer opens with "My son," and the IFs start coming. Friend, he is about to stack up conditions like cookie trays on a cooling rack.

cards.question: The writer's very first IF is about his own words. What does he hope the son will do with them?

cards.text: He tells the son to keep his commandments hidden inside, and the IFs keep stacking up: turn your ear to wisdom, point your heart at understanding. This man writes instructions like a recipe card, and he is NOT on the last step yet.

cards.question: The son is told to truly call out to ___ and lift his voice to understanding.

cards.text: Then the writer tells the son just how hard to look for wisdom. Not a casual look, friend, this is flipping every couch cushion for your car keys when you are ALREADY LATE.

cards.question: The writer paints a picture of how hard to look for wisdom. He says to search for it the way people search for what?

answers.text: Grain in a time of famine

cards.question: All those IFs lead to one big THEN. If the son seeks wisdom like treasure, he will discern the fear of the LORD. What else will he discover?

cards.text: Now here's the twist: the son does all that digging, but he doesn't make the treasure. He just brings the shovel.

cards.question: The son does the searching, but the ___ is the one who gives wisdom.

cards.text: The LORD stores up sound wisdom for the upright, like a cookie box set aside with your name on it. And to those who walk with integrity, He is a shield.

cards.question: The LORD guards the paths of justice.

cards.text: And here comes ANOTHER then. The son will discern righteousness and justice and equity.

cards.question: Once he finds wisdom, the son will be able to tell which paths are good.

cards.text: Wisdom doesn't just knock on the door, friend. It walks right into the son's heart, unpacks its bags and puts its toothbrush by the sink.

cards.question: Once wisdom enters the son's heart, knowledge will feel like a heavy load on his soul.
With wisdom moved into the son's heart, what will watch over him and guard him?

cards.text: Discretion and understanding aren't standing guard for decoration, friend. They're there to deliver the son from the way of evil, and from the man whose talk is perverse.

Then there are the ones who walk off the straight paths and into the ways of darkness. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a dark junk drawer waiting for the light, and these people are walking INTO the dark?!

cards.question: The people walking in the ways of darkness enjoy doing evil.
The people who leave the straight paths walk paths that are ___ and ways that are devious.

cards.text: The rescue list keeps going: the son will be rescued "from the forbidden woman, from the stranger with seductive words…" She has walked away from the partner of her youth.

cards.question: Besides walking away from the partner of her youth, what does the forbidden woman forget?

answers.text: The way back to her city

cards.text: Then the writer gets very serious about where her house leads. Lean in, friend.

cards.question: Where does the forbidden woman's house sink?
People who go to the forbidden woman can come back and find the paths of life again.

cards.text: So where does all this guarding leave the son? Somewhere much better, friend, on a road where your GPS never has to say "recalculating."

cards.question: With wisdom guarding him, the son will follow in the ways of the ___ and keep to the paths of the righteous.

cards.text: The writer closes with two groups of people and two VERY different endings. Friend, this is the part of the movie where I'm yelling at the screen, "PICK THE RIGHT DOOR!"

cards.question: What happens to the upright and the blameless?

answers.text: They inhabit the land and remain in it
They leave the land for a far country
They rule over the land as kings

cards.question: In the end, the wicked will be cut off from the land.
